label: Integrated digital business strategy
definition: An explicit, business-integrated digital strategy that fuses IT and business strategy, has a multi-year horizon, a governing role over initiatives, and is openly communicated.

label: Continuous business-IT alignment
definition: Business-IT strategic alignment treated as a continuous, multidimensional, dynamically sustained process (strategic fit, functional integration, cross-domain and cross-unit alignment), not a one-time fit.

label: Operating-model choice & foundation for execution
definition: A deliberate operating-model decision (diversification/coordination/replication/unification) and a business model that bridges strategy formulation to execution design.

label: Value creation, capture & business-model renewal
definition: Explicit value-creation/value-capture logic (appropriability, complementary assets) and business-model transformation as a precondition for monetizing digital innovation.

label: Strategic focus & attention allocation
definition: Deliberate, non-compensatory allocation of strategic attention across transformation domains; avoiding spreading digital commitment too thin.

label: Decision-rights architecture
definition: Explicit design of IT/transformation decision rights: which decisions exist (principles, architecture, infrastructure, business needs, investment), who holds them, matched to decision type and performance goal.

label: Coordinated governance mechanism deployment
definition: Structures, processes, and relational mechanisms deployed as a coordinated set with sufficient practice maturity; relational mechanisms and principled commitment are necessary, not optional.

label: Governance transparency & shared understanding
definition: Transparency of governance mechanisms and manager/stakeholder understanding and awareness of them as a leading predictor of governance performance.

label: Durable, actively designed governance
definition: Governance that is actively designed, simple, educated-about, and redesigned infrequently; frequent restructuring signals rather than cures ineffectiveness.

label: Federated governance balance
definition: Deliberate balance of centralized standards with decentralized domain autonomy (federated/bimodal designs), including its known latency and compromise costs.

label: Context-contingent governance design
definition: Governance designs contingent on size, maturity, risk appetite, sector, and optimized performance dimension; no one-size-fits-all model.

label: Board & top-leadership governance engagement
definition: Board-level and executive-level engagement with distinct mandates; top-leadership support enabling principled governance commitment.

label: Accountability, ownership & aligned incentives
definition: Clear single-point accountability and ownership plus incentives (including soft/recognition-based) aligned to transformation and standardization goals.

label: Governance of decentralized & business-led IT
definition: Governance for decentralized development (shadow IT to business-managed IT, citizen development, autonomous delivery teams): information symmetry, legitimacy, risk-tiered proportionate control, and enacted decision-right realignment.

label: Strategic IT portfolio governance
definition: Elevating strategic IT-project prioritization to the senior governing body with boundary-spanning coordination structures (portfolio office) and architecture-guided investment oversight.

label: Managed IT-standards lifecycle
definition: A dedicated steering structure, lifecycle model, incentive linkage, and proactive communication for in-company IT standards.

label: EA artifacts as usable boundary objects
definition: EA artifacts designed for cognitive fit and usability, acting as boundary objects, decision-propagation and knowledge-conservation instruments across hierarchy and functions.

label: Stakeholder participation & shared language in EA
definition: Active stakeholder participation, communication richness, and a shared business-IT language in EA development; their absence is the most cross-validated EA obstacle.

label: Architecture transparency of complexity & dependencies
definition: EA-provided transparency over complexity, dependencies, and actual (not idealized) structure as the basis for readiness assessment, scoping, and modifiability/change-cost control.

label: EA as a service with actionable artifacts
definition: EA delivered as a continuous service (not a document product) whose diagnostic, actionable, strategic-insight artifacts drive decision quality.

label: EA quality & strategy-driven EA process
definition: Validated EA quality attributes and a top-down, business-strategy-driven, future-oriented EA process as the leading quality indicator.

label: EA function design & placement
definition: EA function sizing, specialization, structure, and corporate placement matched to organization size, diversification, and required authority.

label: Stage-appropriate EA capability development
definition: EA practice maturity as a staged, non-skippable progression whose level conditions planning paths, decision quality, and which conditions matter most.

label: Dynamic EA capabilities
definition: EA sensing/mobilizing/transforming as a dynamic capability driving alignment and process innovation, including continuous EA-grounded sense-making.

label: Mediated, configuration-dependent EA value realization
definition: EA value realized indirectly through mediators (alignment, process innovation, decision-making), gated by conversion factors and equifinal EAM configurations, moderated by organizational context.

label: Agile, iterative EA practice
definition: Agile, business-focused, iterative EA (backlogs, interim states, integrator roles) replacing waterfall IT-centric EA that is structurally mismatched with digital transformation.

label: Composable, modular platform architecture
definition: Composable/modular, loosely coupled, federated platform architectures (packaged business capabilities, data mesh, vendor-agnostic mappings) enabling scaling and lower-cost change.

label: Business capability modeling & capability-based planning
definition: Business capability maps, value streams, and capability-based planning as the method for identifying, prioritizing, and scoping transformation initiatives.

label: Architecture governance, conformance & compliance
definition: Architecture governance and coherence: project conformance, formal/informal control portfolios, compliance layers/roles, automated verification, and reconciliation with portfolio management.

label: Cross-organizational & ecosystem architecture
definition: Extended enterprise architecture spanning legally distinct organizations and ecosystems, with explicit viability factors and its typical lead-organization asymmetry.

label: Modeling foundations for traceability & automated alignment
definition: EA modeling extensions (motivation modeling, typed inter-layer links, ontologies, patterns, layer extensions, process mining) enabling strategy-to-operations traceability and automatable alignment evaluation.

label: AI-augmented EA practice & its governance
definition: GenAI/AI integration into EA practice: role shift to curator/validator, four readiness domains, maturity-staged AI governance, and known reliability limits.

label: EA adoption readiness & institutional context
definition: EA adoption drivers and preconditions: regulatory pressure, sponsorship, co-investment, institutional articulation, staged obstacle resolution, and adoption-readiness elements.

label: Data quality & data governance foundation
definition: Data quality management and data governance (including security and common data infrastructure) as a foundational enabling condition; data management is a leading barrier category when absent.

label: Technology & infrastructure readiness
definition: Robust, flexible, integrable technology infrastructure and analytics capability, with integration capability mediating readiness to value.

label: Balanced socio-technical progression
definition: People, organizational, and governance dimensions established alongside (or before) technology investment; organizational integration outweighs technological sophistication.

label: Digital sensing capability
definition: Systematic sensing: scouting, scenario planning, cross-industry brokering, inside-out infrastructure sensing, and deliberate absorptive filtering.

label: Digital seizing capability & strategic agility
definition: Rapid seizing of sensed opportunities: strategic agility, speed, scale elasticity, solution-centric restructuring; bounded by managerial decision biases.

label: Digital transforming capability
definition: Ecosystem navigation, structural redesign, and maturity-building capability to institutionalize transformation.

label: Capability orchestration & sequenced change
definition: Orchestrating dynamic capabilities through structured change management, stage-appropriate sequencing, pacing, and contingent configuration of levers.

label: Structural ambidexterity & adaptive organizational forms
definition: Adaptive structures: autonomous/flat units, separation-vs-integration decisions, experimentation tracks, recursive centralization-decentralization recalibration, and agility paths.

label: Pre-built surge, learning & adaptive-governance capacity
definition: Resilience/antifragility built through IT service quality, governance maturity, adaptive governance behavior, surge capacity, and learning; disruption alone does not create it.

label: Executive support & cross-functional collaboration
definition: Sustained executive sponsorship combined with cross-functional collaboration as the pervasive capability-building enabler (most recurrent condition in the corpus).

label: Dedicated digital leadership roles with real authority
definition: CDO/transformation units, cross-functional governance bodies, and digital leadership that only work when granted genuine enterprise-level authority and executive unity.

label: Workforce digital skills & role redefinition
definition: Digital skill development, role redefinition, talent acquisition, and management digital competence; skills consistently lag strategy maturity.

label: Genuine employee participation & sentiment
definition: Employee participation grounded in sentiment, autonomy/competence/relatedness needs, and wellbeing; participation cannot be engineered and misread emotions masquerade as resistance.

label: Managerial readiness micro-foundations
definition: Individual managerial readiness (strategy, structure, technology dispositions) as a distinct micro-foundational precondition not reducible to organizational readiness.

label: Stakeholder trust & psychological ownership
definition: Trust and psychological ownership as the mechanism securing buy-in and governance effectiveness, built via bi-directional communication and positive engagement.

label: Digital organizational culture
definition: Risk tolerance, experimentation, innovation mindset, collaboration, learning, and information openness as cultural substrate; core values filter transformation decisions.

label: Collective organizational change readiness
definition: Shared change valence and change efficacy as a collective property, with capacity (resources/structure) as a distinct antecedent.

label: Structured change management & change communication
definition: Change narratives, cascading sponsorship, frame-of-reference communication, and momentum-building decomposition as the delivery mechanism of change readiness.

label: Multi-dimensional readiness/maturity assessment architecture
definition: Readiness/maturity assessed across validated multi-dimensional structures with staged levels, dimension-level (not only aggregate) evaluation, and hard+soft+context domains.

label: Assessment validity & multi-perspective measurement
definition: Valid measurement through multi-assessor panels, employee-vs-leadership triangulation, validated instruments, and interview-corrected self-assessment.

label: Assessment-to-action linkage
definition: Converting assessment into action: KPIs, thresholds, recommendation engines, roadmaps, continuous reassessment procedures, and accessible self-service tooling.

label: Readiness as distinct construct from maturity
definition: Readiness (behaviors, willingness, cyclical system) formally distinguished from maturity (implementation status) as an assessment precondition.

label: SME resource & capability constraints
definition: SME resource, skill, and R&D constraints with substitution mechanisms (intermediaries, collaboration) and SME-adapted models instead of scaled-down large-firm approaches.

label: Ecosystem partnerships & strategic sourcing
definition: Disciplined ecosystem partnering, vendor co-design, external mediation, and explicit build-vs-outsource competence decisions.

label: Sectoral, regional & institutional contingency
definition: Transformation approaches conditioned by sector, region, regulation, and institutional context; uniform strategies and imported models underperform.

label: Framework pragmatism over framework compliance
definition: Treating EA frameworks as adaptable means rather than prescriptive ends: best-practice capability without named frameworks, avoiding rigidity, pragmatic trade-offs, lightweight principles.

label: Committed, adaptive investment & resourcing
definition: Sufficient committed investment paired with articulated vision, balanced technology-and-human-capital allocation, and funding models matched to transformation dynamics (portfolio/usage-based rather than stage-gate only).
